prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
I am here today to answer the allegations before this committee fully and truthfully.

Let the record show that I did not, as has been alleged, leave the game at the start of the fourth quarter. I left my seat with exactly 11:43 remaining on the clock, during a television timeout, following a defensive holding penalty. This was not "the start" of the fourth quarter, and to characterize it as such is a deliberate misrepresentation of the timeline.

Furthermore, the implication that I left to "beat traffic" impugns my character and my loyalty to the principles that make this pastime great. I reject that premise entirely. My departure was a strategic relocation to the parking lot, where I intended to listen to the final minutes on AM radio while conducting a preemptive tactical assessment of the egress patterns. This was not an abandonment of the game; it was an advanced logistical operation to ensure my post-game transition was as efficient as possible.

I have dedicated countless hours to this franchise, often staying well past the final whistle, through overtime, and even through the post-game handshake lines, long after the fair-weather observers have departed. To suggest that I am somehow un-American for optimizing my exit strategy during a non-critical stoppage in play is a smear campaign orchestrated by those who don't understand the difference between fandom and fanaticism.

I am a patriot who believes in preparedness. I will not apologize for being ready to move when the moment is right. I stand by my record, and I stand by my decision.
